Tabulate columns

Source: R/tab.R
tab.Rd

Enhanced count().

  • tab() - Tabulates variable(s) simultaneously, similar to count().

  • tab1() - Tabulates variable(s) one by one.

  • tab2() - Cross-tabulates two variables, like Stata's tab x y. With three or more variables it returns every pairwise table, like Stata's tab2 x y z.

Each takes .total = TRUE to add "Total" rows (and, for tab2(), a "total" column). fre(), fre1() and fre2() are shortcuts for tab(.total = TRUE), tab1(.total = TRUE) and tab2(.total = TRUE), named after Stata's fre. xtab() is an alias of tab2().

The functions return data by default. With totals, rich output is available from fre(), fre1() and fre2() with .type = "flextable" when the optional flextable package is installed.

Usage

tab(
  .data,
  ...,
  .by = NULL,
  .desc = FALSE,
  .group_order = c("keys", "frequency"),
  .total = FALSE,
  .wt = NULL,
  .wt_type = c("frequency", "analytic")
)

tab1(
  .data,
  ...,
  .by = NULL,
  .desc = FALSE,
  .type = c("list", "tibble"),
  .group_order = c("keys", "frequency"),
  .total = FALSE,
  .wt = NULL,
  .wt_type = c("frequency", "analytic")
)

tab2(
  .data,
  ...,
  .by = NULL,
  .flip = FALSE,
  .total = FALSE,
  .type = c("auto", "tibble", "flextable"),
  .wt = NULL,
  .wt_type = c("frequency", "analytic"),
  .chi2 = FALSE
)

xtab(
  .data,
  ...,
  .by = NULL,
  .flip = FALSE,
  .total = FALSE,
  .type = c("auto", "tibble", "flextable"),
  .wt = NULL,
  .wt_type = c("frequency", "analytic"),
  .chi2 = FALSE
)

fre2(
  .data,
  ...,
  .by = NULL,
  .flip = FALSE,
  .type = c("auto", "tibble", "flextable"),
  .wt = NULL,
  .wt_type = c("frequency", "analytic"),
  .chi2 = FALSE
)

fre(
  .data,
  ...,
  .by = NULL,
  .desc = FALSE,
  .type = c("auto", "tibble", "flextable"),
  .group_order = c("keys", "frequency"),
  .wt = NULL,
  .wt_type = c("frequency", "analytic")
)

fre1(
  .data,
  ...,
  .by = NULL,
  .desc = FALSE,
  .type = c("list", "tibble", "flextable"),
  .group_order = c("keys", "frequency"),
  .wt = NULL,
  .wt_type = c("frequency", "analytic")
)

Arguments

.data

An in-memory data frame, tibble, or data.table. Collect lazy tables before tabulating. tab(), tab1(), fre() and fre1() also accept an atomic vector, tabulated as a tibble column named value; omit selectors and .by in this form. tab2() needs a data frame. All spatial sfc geometry columns are excluded before attribute tabulation; geometry columns cannot be selected as measured variables or grouping keys.

...

<tidy-select> or <data-masking> Variables to tabulate.

Both tidyselect (e.g., starts_with()) and data masking (e.g., x_sq = x^2) are supported. See examples below.

.by

Optional grouping columns, selected with tidyselect. For tab(), tab1(), fre() and fre1(), NULL inherits existing group_by() groups; an explicit selection replaces them. Grouping columns are not measured variables. For tab2() and fre2(), .by returns a list with one cross-table per group, named like "g = a", as Stata's by g: tab x y; grouped data are not split without .by. tab2() does not accept .desc or .group_order.

.desc

If TRUE, sort categories by descending count within each group (missing categories stay last). To order the .by group blocks by size, use .group_order = "frequency".

.group_order

Group block order for one-way and joint tables. "keys" retains key order; "frequency" orders by descending observation count, including missing measured values. Missing grouping keys appear last and ties follow key order. .desc controls categories within each group independently.

.total

A single TRUE or FALSE. If TRUE, add "Total" rows: tab(.total = TRUE) is fre() and tab1(.total = TRUE) is fre1(). tab2(.total = TRUE) is fre2() and adds a total row and a total column. Flextable output from tab2() requires totals.

.wt

Optional weights: a numeric column of .data (or a vector with one value per row), like Stata's [fweight]/[aweight]. Rows with a missing weight are excluded with a message; negative weights are an error. When ... is omitted, the weight column is not tabulated itself.

.wt_type

"frequency" (default) or "analytic". Frequency weights count each row w times, so n is the sum of the weights, as in dplyr::count(wt =); non-integer weights are allowed. Analytic weights (Stata's [aweight], suitable for sampling weights) are rescaled within each .by group to sum to the number of rows, so n stays on the sample scale. Percentages are the same under both types.

.type

Output type. tab1() and fre1() default to a list of tables; fre(), tab2() and fre2() default to "auto", preserving the input container. Explicit "tibble" always returns a plain tibble. Explicit "flextable" output requires the optional flextable package.

.flip

A single TRUE or FALSE. If TRUE, swap the rows and columns of the cross-table.

.chi2

A single TRUE or FALSE. If TRUE, tab2() reports Pearson's chi-square test of independence and Cramer's V, like Stata's tab x y, chi2 V. See Details.

Value

A table, a list of tables, or an explicitly requested flextable. Default tables preserve the input's data.frame, tibble, or data.table container, including each table in a list. Results are ungrouped, with grouping keys retained as columns where applicable. Supported preview settings persist unless an explicit output type is requested. Other subclasses are not reconstructed on these newly shaped tables. Input data are not modified.

Details

Counts and percentages

For tab(), tab1(), fre() and fre1(), n counts observations. percent and cum are percentages from zero to 100 using all observations within each group; cum follows the displayed category order. valid and valid_cum use only observations with no missing measured values. Missing group keys are retained and do not make an otherwise observed value invalid. Missing measured categories have NA valid percentages and appear last.

Totals

fre() and fre1() append a "Total" row within each group and may add "Valid Total" and "Missing Total" subtotals. In tables with up to five measured variables, the final measured column is converted to character to hold these labels; wider tables use a separate total label column. Displayed value labels can coincide for distinct underlying values, or with an observed "Total" category. Counts remain separate; use tab() or tab1() when original category values and types are needed.

List columns and empty selections

tab() counts list-column values by their complete identities without flattening their contents. Selecting no measured variables returns no rows: tab() and fre() retain their count and percentage columns and any grouping keys; tab1() and fre1() return an empty list by default or an empty table with .type = "tibble". tab2() returns an empty table when no variables are selected and errors when only one is. With three or more, it returns a list of every pairwise table, named like "x x y", each with the same options. With no selected variables, tab2(..., .type = "flextable") errors because rich cross-tabulation requires two selected variables.

Cross-tabulation

Cross-tabulation keeps category names unchanged. Categories may match the original variable names. Column categories follow their values: factor levels in order, other types ascending, with missing values last. A category matching the combined row-header name, or literal "NA" alongside a missing column category, causes a name-collision error. With tab2(.total = TRUE), the column category "total" is reserved for marginal totals; recode it first or omit the totals. The final row of tab2(.total = TRUE) is the marginal total, labelled "total"; an observed row category with the same label remains a separate row. Blank column categories use "<empty>", with the smallest unused numeric suffix when that header is already taken. Logical cross-tabulation axes follow FALSE, TRUE, then missing values.

Chi-square test

With .chi2 = TRUE, tab2() tests the categories shown in the table, including missing ones (filter them out first to exclude them), and drops rows or columns with no observations. It prints Pearson's chi-square, its degrees of freedom, the p-value and Cramer's V as a message, and stores them as a one-row tibble in attr(result, "chi2") with columns statistic, df, p_value, cramers_v and n. Flextable output adds them as a footer. As in Stata, V keeps its sign in 2 x 2 tables. The test matches chisq.test(correct = FALSE). Frequency weights are treated as counts; analytic weights are an error, because a design-based test such as survey::svychisq() is needed for sampling weights.

Combined output

Combined tab1() output uses character values when factor types cannot be combined; each variable's category order is retained. List output preserves the original category classes.

If the output tibble has many rows, consider using print() to display the output.

See also

Other tabulation functions: pwcorr()

Examples

# tabulate the 8th column
tab(dplyr::starwars, 8)
#> # A tibble: 5 × 6
#>   sex                n percent   cum valid valid_cum
#>   <chr>          <int>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 female            16   18.4   18.4 19.3       19.3
#> 2 hermaphroditic     1    1.15  19.5  1.20      20.5
#> 3 male              60   69.0   88.5 72.3       92.8
#> 4 none               6    6.90  95.4  7.23     100  
#> 5 NA                 4    4.60 100   NA         NA  

# tabulate the "sex" column
tab(dplyr::starwars, sex)
#> # A tibble: 5 × 6
#>   sex                n percent   cum valid valid_cum

# Weighted frequencies, like Stata's tab x [fw=w] or [aw=w]

tab(survey, edu, .wt = w)

#>   edu       n percent   cum valid valid_cum

#> 1 high    2.5    55.6  55.6  55.6      55.6
#> 2 low     2      44.4 100    44.4     100  
tab(survey, edu, .wt = w, .wt_type = "analytic")

# One cross-table per group, like Stata's by species: tab sex gender
tab2(dplyr::starwars, sex, gender, .by = species) |> head(2)
#> $`species = Aleena`
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>   `sex \\ gender` masculine
#>   <chr>               <int>
#> 1 male                    1
#> 
#> $`species = Besalisk`
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>   `sex \\ gender` masculine
#>   <chr>               <int>
#> 1 male                    1
#> 

# Chi-square test of independence, like Stata's tab x y, chi2 V
chi2 <- tab2(dplyr::starwars, sex, gender, .chi2 = TRUE)
#> Pearson chi2(8) = 168.6368   Pr = 0.000
#> Cramer's V = 0.9845
attr(chi2, "chi2")
#> # A tibble: 1 × 5
#>   statistic    df  p_value cramers_v     n
#>       <dbl> <int>    <dbl>     <dbl> <int>
#> 1      169.     8 2.49e-32     0.984    87
